question: Should the browser agent tool gain explicit `download` and `waitfordownload` actions in addition to the merged `/act` download metadata behavior?
rationale: Current main lacks the explicit actions, but the canonical user problem was already fixed by a different API shape, and this PR expands a security-sensitive file-download surface that needs maintainer product intent before merge.

options.title: Refresh and prove explicit actions
options.body: Keep this direction, require a current-main rebase or replacement, remove the changelog edit, and require live managed-browser proof before merge.

options.title: Treat `/act` metadata as sufficient
options.body: Close this PR as superseded if maintainers want one agent-visible download contract instead of adding explicit tool actions.

options.title: Defer browser download API design
options.body: Keep the PR paused while maintainers decide a broader browser download API shape across CLI, control API, and agent tools.

recommendation.title: Refresh and prove explicit actions
recommendation.body: Keep this direction, require a current-main rebase or replacement, remove the changelog edit, and require live managed-browser proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is both the live assignee and the strongest browser plugin/tool history owner in the inspected git history.
